pools.title: Pools
pools.label: Name
pools.description: Members are tried in order. Site permissions still apply. Administrators must ensure equivalent routing policies; failover can reconnect sessions. Inventory does not prove traffic readiness.
pools.prerequisite: Grants are explicit. Enable Allow pools separately in VPN Users; this screen never enables it or grants site access. Only currently authorized, available routes reach clients.

vpnDetail.title: VPN Server Details
vpnDetail.mgmtSaved: Management access saved — the site is now in the Ansible inventory
vpnDetail.mgmtHintUnset: This site has no SSH host recorded, so it is not in the Ansible inventory and cannot be updated by ADM. Set one to adopt it — this does not install anything or open a tunnel.
vpnDetail.mgmtHintSet: Ansible reaches the box at this address to deploy it. Change it if the box moved or a different path opens.
vpnDetail.confirmDelete: Are you sure you want to delete this VPN server?
vpnDetail.confirmDeleteTunnel: Are you sure you want to delete this tunnel?
monitoring.filterHint: Click a server to hide it, or use the focus icon to show only that one.
monitoring.noData: No monitoring data yet. Metrics will appear after the first collection cycle.
monitoring.noVpnData: No VPN server monitoring data yet. Metrics will appear after the first collection cycle.
common.name: Name
vpnUsers.legend: Left icon: authorized on this server. Right icon: may reach that site's LAN devices. Click a name for details.
vpnUsers.lanOnHint: LAN access allowed — click to block
vpnUsers.lanOffHint: LAN access blocked — click to allow
vpnUsers.syncWaiting: Pushed. {{n}} change(s) are waiting for a site that does not answer: {{servers}}. They will be delivered when it is back.
vpnUsers.revokeQueued: Server unreachable — removal will be retried
vpnUsers.revokeWarning: Their account and all its devices on that server are deleted. A WireGuard peer keeps working on its own keys, so leaving the devices behind would not actually revoke anything.
vpnUsers.revokeAlternative: To suspend without deleting devices, turn the account off in its detail view instead.
vpnUsers.usernameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen
vpnUsers.usernameInvalid: Use only a–z, 0–9 and . _ - (not at the start or end, not two in a row). No spaces, accents or Cyrillic.
vpnUsers.usernameLocked: Cannot be changed once the account exists on a server
vpnUsers.passwordHelp: At least {{min}} characters. The user logs in with this.
vpnUsers.newPasswordHelp: Leave empty to keep the current one
vpnUsers.packageHint: Hand this over to the user. ADM stores only a hash, so it cannot show the password again later.
vpnUsers.routeChooseHint: This site publishes several Direct routes — click to choose
vpnUsers.routeNonePublished: This site publishes no Direct routes
admins.title: Administrators
admins.superadminHelp: Full access, including servers, provisioning and these accounts.
admins.scopedAdminHelp: May only manage VPN users on the servers selected below.
admins.passwordOnce: This password is shown once and is not stored. Copy it now.
admins.deleteBody: Delete the account {{username}}? Their VPN users are not affected.
admins.roleExplainer: A server admin manages VPN users on their own servers only. They cannot register servers, provision, see monitoring, or change a user who also belongs to a server outside their scope.
setupVpn.title: Set up a new VPN server
setupVpn.explainer: ADM connects over SSH, joins the box to the management network so it stays reachable whatever happens next, installs Proxima, and then claims it. The SSH password is discarded once that succeeds.
setupVpn.sshUserHelp: A sudo user; Debian blocks root by password
setupVpn.sshPasswordHelp: Used once to get in, then discarded. Leave empty if the box already has ADM's key.
setupVpn.running: Installing. This takes several minutes — Docker images are built and the AmneziaWG module is compiled on the machine.
setupVpn.done: Installed and claimed. The server is now managed from here.
setupVpn.failed: Install failed. The log below shows where; the server stays registered so you can retry.
vpnServer.tokenExpired: Site token expired on {{date}} — every call fails until the site is re-claimed
vpnServer.tokenExpiring: Site token expires on {{date}} — renewal is pending
panelAccess.explainer: The columns on the right decide who can sign into each site's own Proxima panel. They use the password they already have here — nothing separate to issue or remember. This is not the same as the servers column: that one only decides whose accounts they may edit in ADM.
panelAccess.pendingRevoke: Waiting to be removed from this site
panelAccess.retry: {{count}} change(s) have not reached their site — retry
panelAccess.partial: Saved, but a site could not be reached: {{detail}}
panelAccess.revokeBody: {{username}} will no longer be able to sign into {{server}}. Their account there is deleted; anything else about them is untouched.
setupVpn.panelAdminNote: You become this server's panel admin, signing in with the password you already use here. Nothing is generated and nothing has to be handed over. Give someone else access later from Operators.
setupVpn.vpnSubnetHelp: As set on the router, e.g. 10.17.17.0/24
setupVpn.lanSubnetHelp: The range the MikroTik hands out
setupVpn.takenRanges: Already in use — anything overlapping these is refused:
setupVpn.vpnEndpointHelp: Where clients dial in — the site's public address and forwarded port. Left empty, peer configs point at this machine's LAN address, which only works on site.
services.title: {{name}} — what is running
services.missing: Configured but not listening: {{list}}. Clients relying on these will fail.
services.unexpected: Listening but not part of Proxima: {{list}}. Worth knowing before the box ships.
services.notObserved: The socket list could not be read, so this shows only what the configuration expects — not what is actually running.
mgmt.title: Management tunnel
mgmt.explainer: The node dials out to ADM, so management no longer depends on its public address being reachable.
mgmt.installHint: Run this on the node. Its provider console works even when SSH does not.
